title: ForgeOps War Room: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Transit Map Office. Keep it, take Impeccable's pick, or re-roll.

options.label: Transit Map Office
options.lineage: 1970s modernist subway diagrams, drawn as an office floor plan
options.thesis: The office is a network map: desks are stations, each agent owns a route color, and a question travels the line to a colleague's station.
options.viewport: The whole floor as one map: seven desk-stations on colored lines, an interchange evidence wall at the center, the RCA terminus, and the chat bar docked right asking "What's broken?".
options.risk: Can read as a diagram rather than an office if the desks and figures are drawn too abstractly.

raised.raise: Route colors are flat, fully committed fields with no gradients or glow; every state change is an instant color swap.
Evidence cards hang on leader lines from the stations that found them; supporting and contradicting links are drawn as distinct line styles.
One warm value is reserved for the live incident clock; nothing else on the floor uses it.
The map is a fixed stage that never reflows; chat, evidence detail and approval change around it.
Timestamps, durations and tool calls set in one tight tabular monospace column in the live feed.

options.label: Mission Control Floor
options.lineage: 1960s flight control rooms: flight director plus specialist console rows
options.thesis: A flight director and rows of specialist consoles on shared voice loops; agents talk on loops and the big front screen carries the plan.
options.viewport: Tiered console rows facing a front screen with the incident and plan; the director console at the back, chat as the loop panel.
options.risk: Familiar: control-room metaphors are where most incident tools land, and it pulls toward a dark cockpit look.

options.label: Starship Elbow Panel
options.thesis: Every desk as a pastel pill bank inside sweeping elbow frames.
options.viewport: Elbow frames sweeping around desk banks.
options.risk: Reads as sci-fi costume, the game-like feel you ruled out.
options.case: Fuses poorly: founders do not identify an incident with a starship set.
options.kept: Flat, fully committed color with instant state swaps.

options.label: Tensegrity Force Diagram
options.lineage: kinetic tension sculpture and force diagrams
options.thesis: Evidence as a network of tension and counterforce.
options.viewport: A strut network with findings pinned to nodes.
options.risk: Abstract; the office and its people disappear.
options.case: Fuses partly: support versus contradiction maps well, the office does not.
options.kept: Findings pinned on leader lines; support and contradiction as distinct line states.

options.label: Nixie Laboratory Counter
options.thesis: Every count as glowing digits in glass.
options.viewport: Tube banks for elapsed time and counts.
options.case: Fuses poorly: nothing to say about desks talking to each other.
options.kept: A single warm accent reserved for the one live value.

options.label: CD-ROM Console
options.thesis: A fixed machine frame with content changing in a window.
options.viewport: A console framing a small live window.
options.case: Fuses poorly: bevels add noise during an incident.
options.kept: A fixed stage that never reflows.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Barcode fields and monospace numerics in pure black and white.
options.viewport: A data wall of the investigation's numbers.
options.risk: Strobing and abstraction work against calm.
options.case: Fuses poorly: agents and their conversation vanish.
options.kept: One tight tabular monospace column for times and calls.

canonCard.label: Incident dashboard standard
canonCard.thesis: Timeline, agent status cards and an evidence list, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Status cards per agent above a live timeline, chat on the right.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every incident tool; the office idea is lost.
